AUTHOR: Sung
TITLE: Vision based real-time fish detection using convolutional neural network
REGION: NOAA 'Labeled Fishes in the Wild' dataset (location not stated in paper); Ulleungdo Island, Republic of Korea
DATA: NOAA Fisheries Labeled Fishes in the Wild (929 images) + own ROV images from Ulleungdo Island (983 images)
V_EV: Sec. I / Fig. 1: 'Example of Underwater image that shows low light, high noise, and haze effect.'
D2: 829 train / 100 test (NOAA images); all 983 Ulleungdo images used for training
D_EV: Sec. IV.A: 'we divided them into two groups; 829 images for training and 100 images for testing.'
R_EV: Sec. V.B: 'we tested the network with 100 fish images of NOAA dataset.' (Ulleungdo video shown only qualitatively, Fig. 6b)
E_EV: Table III: 'Classification Accuracy ... Sensitivity 93% Specificity 62% IOU 65.2% FPS 16.7' (detection metrics only)
ARCH: YOLO (v1-style, 24 convolutional + 2 fully connected layers); baseline HOG+SVM sliding window
METR: sensitivity, specificity, mean IoU, processing FPS; PR and ROC curves vs HOG+SVM
NOTE: Split is at image level (829/100 NOAA images) but the word 'random' is not used; the NOAA images are frames from ROV video so frame-level leakage is possible and not discussed. PR and ROC curves (Figs. 8-9) are shown for method comparison, but no detection confidence threshold is reported, so C_ALL = NR. Ulleungdo video result is qualitative only (Fig. 6b) and those images were all in training. 16.7 FPS is processing speed, not video frame rate.
